title: Rapid mini-canary blueprint and field journal — 2026-06
content:
Purpose:
Quick, low-risk canary approach for small rolling changes (eg. kernel swap, batching weight tweak, routing policy change) that need fast validation across production telemetry without full staged rollouts. This doc is a compact blueprint + a field journal capturing a dry run from 2026-05-28 and notes for follow-ups.

Scope / when to use:
- Low surface-area changes that are network/serving-runtime adjacent (kernel selection, batching/kv-cache tweaks, quantization params)
- Deploys expected to be backward-compatible at network/API level
- When we need faster post-merge validation than full 7/14-day canary lanes
- Not suitable for model architecture changes or non-backwards-compatible API changes

High-level cadence (mini-canary):
- T0: Deploy to 2% traffic lane (mini-lane-1) for 30 minutes
- T0+30m: Automated checks pass -> expand to 10% (mini-lane-2) for 60 minutes
- T0+90m: If stable, expand to 30% and monitor for 3 hours
- T0+4.5h: If stable, full rollout (or follow dedicated phased rollout plan)
- Abort/rollback window remains open at each expansion checkpoint

Preflight checklist (to be completed before scheduling T0):
- [ ] PR merged with release build artifacts produced (link in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Canary config created in console (route: rapid-mini-canary-<YYYYMMDD>)
- [ ] Observability dashboard pinned (latency p50/p95/p99, request error rate, token/sec, cost-per-token estimate)
- [ ] Smoke test suite updated to include short generative prompts and embedding checks
- [ ] Prefix/KV cache-seed plan defined for common traffic paths (seeds list attached in Confluence)
- [ ] Rollback and emergency contact roster notified and on-call for the window
- [ ] Rate-limits, quotas, and burst policies reviewed to avoid throttling false positives

Automated gating signals (pass/fail rules):
- Latency: p95 increase <= 15% vs baseline for the same time window
- Error rate: client-visible 4xx/5xx increase <= 0.5% absolute (or 2x baseline if baseline <0.25%)
- Model-quality quick checks: BLEU/EM-like surrogate prompt set no regression > 2% (approx metric used for smoke)
- Throughput/cost: token/sec within expected range; cost-per-token degradation flagged if +20%
- KV cache warmup: prefix hit-rate reaches >60% within the first 15 minutes for seeded paths
- Any alert firing on service-level SLOs is immediate fail

Manual checks at each gate (owner in parentheses):
- 00m owner: verify rollout route and traffic split (Release engineer - Diego)
- 10m owner: quick sampling of generated outputs for hallucination/regression (Product PM - Asha)
- 30m owner: validate telemetry dashboard and lint for anomaly graphs (Observability - Markus)
- Expansion decision: consensus in release-ops channel and thumbs-up from on-call (screenshot decision)

Rollback decision matrix:
- Immediate rollback if: p95 latency > 2x baseline OR error rate increase > 1% absolute OR smoke prompts show clear quality regression on multiple prompts
- Consider partial rollback (back to previous split) if: sustained latency p95 uplift >15% but <2x and no correctness regressions
- Post-rollback: capture diffs (telemetry, sampled responses, kernel selection logs) and open an RCA ticket with priority P0/P1 depending on customer impact

Dry run notes (2026-05-28) — field journal:
- Summary: Ran mini-canary on a test traffic slice (non-prod) to exercise the expansion cadence and observability gating.
- Observations:
  * KV cache warmup behaved as expected for seeded prefixes; hit-rate reached 65% at T+12m.
  * Autoscaler triggered an additional worker at ~T+22m under a synthetic traffic ramp; scale-up latency ~45s which caused a transient p99 spike — recommend pre-warming policy change for mini lanes.
  * Small latency bump at T+7m (~10% p95) correlated with a kernel-selection fallback path on a subset of older GPUs. Captured kernel logs in PR #987.
  * No functional regressions in sampled prompt set; two prompts showed slightly altered tokenization causing output length change (tracked in RELEASE-321).
- Actions from dry run:
  1) Add 'pre-warm hint' to canary config to reduce scale-up p99 spike (owner: Markus)
  2) Expand kernel compatibility metrics to include GPU microcode version and map to fallback frequency (owner: Eng Applied ML)
  3) Add two tokenization edge-cases to smoke set (owner: Product QA - Asha)

Ops playbook (step-by-step at T0):
1) Announce start in #release-ops and tag on-call.
2) Create route with 2% split to new deployment.
3) Trigger synthetic smoke traffic for first 5 minutes and confirm no 5xxs.
4) Mark checkpoint 1 (T+30m) in the runbook and run automated gating job.
5) If gating job passes, expand to 10% and continue monitoring; otherwise rollback to 0% and open incident.
6) During expansion to 30%, increase telemetry sampling to 10% of requests for deeper lineage tracing.
7) After final expansion, keep enhanced sampling for 6 hours and then revert to baseline sampling.

Communication templates (paste into #release-ops when needed):
- Start message: "Starting rapid-mini-canary: <change>, T0=<timestamp>. Route: <route>. Owners: Diego/Asha/Markus. Gate checkpoints at 30m/90m/4.5h. Watch dashboards: <link>"
- Abort message: "Aborting rapid-mini-canary: immediate rollback initiated to previous stable. Reason: <brief reason>. RCA ticket: <url>"

Post-rollout checklist:
- [ ] Confirm expanded telemetry sampling is stable and revert sampling after 6h
- [ ] Archive runbook checkpoint logs to Confluence (attach screenshots of gating job)
- [ ] Tag deployment in release registry with rollout notes and any special flags used
- [ ] If regression observed, open RCA and link to the runbook and telemetry snapshots

Open questions / risk notes:
- How to best simulate customer request heterogeneity in synthetic smoke for mini lanes? (Current synthetic set is biased to small prompts.)
- Is pre-warming for mini-lanes acceptable cost-wise for frequent rollouts? Need cost estimate for a 2% pre-warm per weekday cadence.
- Interaction between rapid-mini-canary and Dedicated capacity pools: ensure we don't cause noisy neighbor effects when applied to dedicated pools.

Follow-ups and owners:
- Markus: add pre-warm toggle and estimate cost (due 2026-06-07)
- Asha: expand smoke prompt set with edge cases and QA signoff (due 2026-06-04)
- Diego: formalize runbook template and add to release-conductor checklist (due 2026-06-06)

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Dry run telemetry snapshot: (attached) -> Confluence page in linked_artifacts
- PR that exercised fallback behavior: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987
- Related ticket: RELEASE-321 (tokenization edge-case)

Field-journal closing note:
This mini-canary blueprint is intentionally compact: the goal is quick validation with tight telemetry gates and explicit manual checks. The dry run surfaced a small set of operational tweaks (pre-warm and kernel mapping) that materially reduce the risk window for expansion. Next iteration will codify the gating job and add a short checklist to the Release Conductor UI so shifts can run this without a Slack full-huddle.

-- Diego (release engineer)
Notes saved: 2026-06-03
